description: WifiHaven Plain support integration (#2199 + #2200, epic #2197): server-signed widget-identity outcomes, household→Plain customer-upsert outcomes, the #2200 Claude responder's webhook outcomes (support_ai_draft_total{outcome,reason} from SupportResponder — dispatched / skipped_unauthenticated / rate_limited / invalid_signature / malformed / disabled / error), and the cloud agent's callback actions (support_agent_action_total{op,outcome} — reply / issue / household_read). All labels are bounded enums (never per-email / per-household / per-thread). The responder runs iff the explicit support.responderEnabled flag is set (#2265 — no dark-by-default; a true flag with missing config refuses to boot); disabled installs count outcomes as disabled and dispatch nothing. See issues #2206, #2200, #2241, #2265. #2419 adds the data-access consent lifecycle (support_consent_total{outcome} — the agent's REQUEST vs the customer's grant/revoke, plus the household-mismatch guard): consent is recorded server-side from the customer's own authenticated action, so the agent can ask but can never self-grant. #2438 adds support_dispatch_total{outcome,transport} — the dispatcher-level cloud-trigger outcome (dispatched / error / disabled) at the transport boundary, isolating a silent non-2xx trigger failure the conflated draft metric can't surface. #2435 adds the `reason` label to support_customer_upsert_total (panel 18): the household→Plain customer mapping can be permanently blocked by Plain's workspace-wide customer-email uniqueness, so `reason` separates a self-healed collision (reconciled) from a BROKEN, non-self-healing mapping (email_collision / permission / schema / tenant_missing) and from a transient miss (error). #2437 adds operator_escalation_total{channel="support",kind,outcome} — the operator-notification funnel behind an escalation — plus the support_agent_action_total ops escalate (the agent's structural handoff) and escalate_mark (the SERVER's Plain addLabels write that makes the handoff visible in the inbox).

panels.title: Widget identity requests (cumulative, issued)
panels.description: sum(support_widget_identity_total{outcome="issued"}) — total server-signed identities issued to authenticated admins. Zero while the widget is dark (no Plain app id / identity secret).

panels.title: Widget identity rate by outcome
panels.description: sum by (outcome) (rate(support_widget_identity_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — issued / no_email (caller has no email to identify — username-only admin) / disabled (Plain widget unconfigured, feature dark). A rising no_email share means admins without an email are opening the app; disabled dominates until the operator provisions the Plain widget keys.

panels.title: Household → Plain customer upsert outcomes
panels.description: sum by (outcome) (rate(support_customer_upsert_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — ok (mapping written to Plain, whether first-try or reconciled) / disabled (Plain write API explicitly off, #2266) / error (Plain returned non-2xx or a GraphQL error; fail-open, the identity response is unaffected). A persistent 'error' share means the household→customer mapping isn't reaching Plain. This panel is the aggregate; the '#2435' panel splits it by reason so a BROKEN, non-self-healing mapping (email_collision / permission / schema / tenant_missing) is distinguishable from a transient miss.

panels.title: Responder webhook outcomes (#2200)
panels.description: sum by (outcome) (rate(support_ai_draft_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — dispatched (a cloud-agent session was created for a UI-originated thread) / email_registered_dispatched (#2307: a NEW inbound email whose From matched a registered household admin, admitted to the AI bound to that household) / email_unregistered_rejected (#2307: a NEW inbound email from an unregistered address got the FIXED static reject — NO Claude call, NO tokens burned) / skipped_unauthenticated (a continuation with no resolvable tenant) / skipped_not_inbound (#2403 loop guard: our own outbound thread.chat_sent reply, a non-customer actor, or a bodyless metadata event — never dispatched) / rate_limited (the per-thread + global dispatch, or the global reject, cost caps fired) / invalid_signature (unsigned or forged webhook — security-relevant, investigate a sustained rate) / malformed / disabled (responder dark) / error (Managed Agents dispatch failed). Emitted by SupportResponder.handleWebhook.

panels.title: Agent callback actions (#2200/#2241)
panels.description: sum by (op, outcome) (rate(support_agent_action_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — the dispatched cloud agent's token-authenticated callbacks: reply (post the AI-attributed reply into the token-bound Plain thread — sent to the customer, autonomous send), issue (file a PII-scrubbed, support-agent-labeled GitHub issue), household_read (the consented single-household summary), consent_request (#2419, the server's fixed data-access prompt), escalate (#2437, the agent handing off to a human) and escalate_mark (the SERVER's Plain addLabels write that makes the handoff visible in the inbox). outcome=denied covers bad/expired tokens AND consent-less household reads; rate_limited is the per-thread/global issue caps; ok_no_link (#2461) is a SUCCESSFUL issue filing whose link we could not read back from GitHub's response — count it WITH ok for filing volume, and if it is the only success value rising, the target repo was likely renamed or transferred (the log line names that cause). Emitted by SupportResponder.

panels.title: Agent-filed issues (24h) — volume alert feed
panels.description: sum(increase(support_agent_action_total{env="$env",op="issue",outcome=~"ok|ok_no_link"}[24h])) — GitHub issues the support agent filed in the last 24h (the #2241 volume-alert feed). The per-thread (3/h) + global (10/h) rate limits cap the ceiling; a value near the cap means the agent is filing aggressively — review the support-agent label on GitHub. Counts BOTH success outcomes (#2461): `ok_no_link` is a real filed issue whose link we could not read back, so excluding it would under-report actual GitHub issues created.

panels.title: Agent sessions dispatched (24h) — cost watch
panels.description: sum(increase(support_ai_draft_total{env="$env",outcome="dispatched"}[24h])) — cloud-agent sessions started in the last 24h. Each session bills API tokens (rough order: $0.10–$0.50/draft on Sonnet 5); the global dispatch cap (50/day) bounds the ceiling. Red at the cap = sustained widget spam or a webhook retry loop — check the rate_limited outcome on the webhook panel.

panels.title: Household → Plain tenant entitlement upsert outcomes (#2240)
panels.description: sum by (outcome) (rate(support_tenant_upsert_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — the household→Plain TENANT write (household name + plan/founding tenant fields), separate from the customer upsert. ok (name + all fields written) / error (tenant upsert failed, or a field write failed). Fail-open, the identity response is unaffected. This panel is the aggregate; the '#2410' panel next to it slices error by reason so a PROVISIONING GAP (permission / schema — needs a fix) is distinguishable from a transient tenant/field hiccup.

panels.title: Entitlement write failures by reason — provisioning-gap watch (#2410)
panels.description: sum by (reason) (rate(support_tenant_upsert_total{env="$env",outcome="error"}[5m])) — WHY the household→Plain entitlement write failed. permission (the machine-user API key lacks the tenantField:* permission — grant it, docs/ops/plain-setup.md §5.1) and schema (the plan/founding tenant-field schemas are not registered in the Plain workspace — register them, docs/ops/plain-setup.md §7.3) are PROVISIONING GAPS: they will NEVER self-heal until fixed, and the API also logs each at ERROR with the fix inline. tenant / field_write are the transient/other bucket (a Plain hiccup — usually self-heals). ALERT on any sustained permission or schema rate; a transient tenant/field_write blip is expected noise.

panels.title: Data-access consent lifecycle (#2419)
panels.description: sum by (outcome) (rate(support_consent_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — the in-conversation data-access consent flow. AGENT side: requested (the agent asked, so the SERVER posted its consent prompt into the thread), request_already_granted, request_rate_limited (per-thread cap), request_disabled / request_error (the Plain write). CUSTOMER side, on POST /api/support/consent: granted, revoked (withdrawn ahead of expiry), revoke_noop (a withdrawal of a grant that was not live — idempotent for the customer, but not a real withdrawal), invalid / expired (a bad or stale consent link), household_mismatch. Bounded enum — never a per-household / per-thread label. Emitted by SupportResponder. Healthy flow: `requested` followed by `granted`; sustained `requested` with no `granted` means customers are not completing the link (check the SPA /support/consent page and that they are signed in). #2476 adds two AGENT-side read outcomes: read_no_scope (a token minted without data scope — the common case) and read_withdrawn (a token that WAS minted with data scope, presented after the customer withdrew: the household read re-reads the grant on every call, so a withdrawal bites on the very next read rather than at token expiry). A rising read_withdrawn means grants are being pulled mid-conversation.

panels.title: Consent links redeemed by the WRONG household (24h) — expect 0
panels.description: sum(increase(support_consent_total{env="$env",outcome="household_mismatch"}[24h])) — a consent link minted for household A presented by a household-B session. Nothing is written when this fires (the grant endpoint refuses it), but a NON-ZERO value means links are being shared or replayed across tenants and deserves a look at the threads involved (#2419 security boundary).

panels.title: Cloud-agent dispatch outcomes (#2438)
panels.description: sum by (outcome, transport) (rate(support_dispatch_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — the dispatcher-level cloud-trigger outcome, measured at the transport boundary (CloudAgentObservability): dispatched (the Managed Agents session / Claude Code Cloud routine trigger returned 2xx) / error (the trigger returned non-2xx or the call threw — the cloud agent NEVER started) / disabled (the responder is dark, #2265; carries no transport). transport ∈ managed-agents (API-credit billed) | claude-code-cloud (subscription billed). This is the series the #2408 go-live gap needed: the webhook panel's 'dispatched' outcome only means a session was ATTEMPTED — a silent non-2xx trigger failure shows up as 'error' HERE and nowhere else. ALERT on any sustained 'error' rate while the responder is enabled (each is a support reply that never went out). Emitted for BOTH audiences from one shared envelope; the press twin is press_dispatch_total on the Press dashboard. #2416: when outcome=error, the 'Support dispatch failures by reason' panel below splits that bucket into config (a permanent 4xx misconfiguration — a dead responder needing a human fix, alert W6) vs transient (a 5xx/transport blip).

panels.title: Thread-history reads — responder context watch (#2430)
panels.description: sum by (outcome) (rate(support_thread_history_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — the per-dispatch Plain thread-timeline read that gives the STATELESS support responder its conversation context (a fresh cloud session fires per inbound message, so without this read the agent answers every follow-up in isolation). PROVISIONING / DRIFT buckets, none of which self-heal — alert on any sustained rate: permission (the Plain machine-user API key lacks thread:read — grant it, docs/ops/plain-setup.md §5.1), schema (Plain rejected the query — a timeline-schema drift), unparsed (Plain returned turn-SHAPED entries — chat/email, not notes or status flips — and NONE parsed into a turn: the actor/entry union shapes drifted). Each of those is also logged at ERROR with the fix inline. NORMAL buckets: ok (the read returned at least one turn — note this measures the READ, not how much CONTEXT the agent got: Plain fires the webhook once the inbound message is already on the timeline, so even a genuine first message normally reads back its own echo, which the API then strips), empty (Plain returned no readable timeline entries at all — rare, NOT the common first-message case), error (a transient miss or timeout — occasional is noise), disabled (the Plain client is unconfigured). The read is FAIL-OPEN — every non-ok outcome degrades to "dispatch with the latest message alone" — so this panel is the only way a permanently context-less responder is visible.

panels.title: Consent grants that dead-ended (24h) — expect 0
panels.description: sum(increase(support_consent_total{env="$env",outcome=~"resume_rate_limited|resume_disabled|resume_error"}[24h])) — #2460: a customer granted data access and the server FAILED to close the loop for them. Every grant emits exactly one resume_* outcome. Benign ones: resumed (the customer's last question was re-dispatched under the new scope — the happy path), resume_no_message (Plain's timeline was unreadable so the fixed server-authored nudge posted instead — check the thread-history panel for a thread:read/timeline:read gap), resume_skipped (a re-confirmed LIVE grant — the idempotency guard doing its job). The three counted HERE are the ones where the customer gets nothing back: resume_rate_limited (the thread hit its dispatch cap — the grant landed, the follow-up did not), resume_disabled (the dispatcher or Plain client is unconfigured), resume_error (the dispatch or the nudge write failed). Sustained non-zero means customers are granting permission and still being left waiting — the exact symptom #2460 fixed.

panels.title: Support dispatch failures by reason — dead-responder watch (#2416)
panels.description: sum by (reason) (rate(support_ai_draft_total{env="$env",outcome="error"}[5m])) — WHY the support cloud agent could not be dispatched. Complements the #2438 'Cloud-agent dispatch outcomes' panel, which counts dispatch attempts by {outcome,transport}: this one splits the ERROR bucket by cause. config = a non-self-healing 4xx at the Anthropic boundary: a revoked/wrong anthropicApiKey (401), a wrong claudeAgentId / claudeEnvironmentId / claudeCodeRoutineId (404), or a STALE hard-coded anthropic-beta header (400). Those NEVER self-heal — the responder is dead until a human rotates the key, fixes the id, or bumps the header, and the API also logs each at ERROR with the fix named inline. transient = transport / timeout / 5xx, plus the 4xx that ARE load/timing signals (408, 429) — expected noise. ALERT on any sustained 'config' rate (warning rule W6, infra/grafana/alerting-rules-warning.tf); ignore isolated 'transient' blips. Dispatch is fail-open by design, so the webhook keeps returning 200 either way.

panels.title: Escalations to a human (#2437)
panels.description: sum by (outcome) (rate(operator_escalation_total{env="$env",channel="support",kind="escalated"}[5m])) — #2437. Every support thread the AI handed off, by how the operator notice landed. A rising rate means the responder is escalating more than expected. Any series that is not `sent` means a human was owed a notice and did not get the email (failed = Resend rejected it, skipped_disabled = the email transport is off, skipped_no_recipient = no wifihaven.email.operatorAddress); the in-Plain needs-human label is the second, independent channel (see the unmarked-threads panel).

panels.title: Escalated threads NOT marked in Plain (24h) — expect 0 (#2437)
panels.description: sum(increase(support_agent_action_total{env="$env",op="escalate_mark",outcome=~"error|disabled"}[24h])) — the server's Plain addLabels write failed, so an escalated thread is INVISIBLE under the needs-a-human inbox filter and the operator is back to reading every thread. Non-zero is a provisioning gap, not a blip: check wifihaven.support.plain.escalationLabelTypeId and that the Plain machine-user API key carries the `label:create` permission (docs/ops/plain-setup.md §5.1).

panels.title: Support escalations handed off (24h) (#2437)
panels.description: sum(increase(operator_escalation_total{env="$env",channel="support",kind="escalated"}[24h])) — how many support conversations the AI handed to a human in the last 24h. Not an error signal: it is the human-workload number, and the counterweight to support_ai_draft_total when asking whether the assistant is resolving enough on its own.

panels.title: Customer↔household mapping by reason — broken-mapping watch (#2435)
panels.description: sum by (reason) (rate(support_customer_upsert_total{env="$env"}[5m])) — HOW the household→Plain customer mapping resolved. ok = upserted on the first try (the common path). reconciled = the household admin's email was already held by a Plain customer with NO externalId (Plain auto-creates one from an inbound support email, #2198), and we bound it onto the household by patching externalId + joining the tenant — a self-healed collision, expected on any household that emailed support before loading the widget. email_collision = that reconcile FAILED for no more specific cause: the mapping is BROKEN and will NEVER self-heal (the email is taken forever), so the household's widget messages resolve no tenantIdentifier and fall through to the email-intake fallback or are dropped as skipped_unauthenticated. permission (the machine-user lacks customer:edit for the upsert, or customerTenantMembership:create for the household-membership join — a reconcile leg attributes these too, not just the primary upsert) and schema (our UpsertCustomerInput no longer matches Plain's schema) are the other non-self-healing PROVISIONING GAPS. ALERT on any sustained email_collision / permission / schema / tenant_missing rate — each is a fix, not a blip, and the API also logs each at ERROR with the fix named inline. tenant_missing = the membership join had no TENANT to join to because the tenant write itself FAILED; do NOT debug it from this panel — the specific cause is on support_tenant_upsert_total{reason=tenant} (panel 9, 'Entitlement write failures by reason'), and this join cannot succeed until that write does. error = the transient/other bucket (including a join whose tenant was merely SKIPPED for want of household context — a degraded repo read the next identity call repairs); disabled = the write API is explicitly off (#2266).

panels.title: Agent callbacks REFUSED at the token check (#2473)
panels.description: sum by (op, reason) (rate(agent_token_rejected_total{env="$env",channel="support"}[5m])) — Every sample is a cloud-agent callback we REFUSED at the token check — an answer that was generated and then thrown away at the door, so the customer/journalist received nothing. token_expired = a token WE minted outlived its TTL: the #2473 failure, where a claude-code-cloud run paused on subscription usage limits and resumed after the token had died. Sustained non-zero token_expired means agentTokenTtlMinutes is again shorter than the transport's real round-trip latency — raise it (api/src/Config.scala, AgentTokenTtl). invalid = malformed or wrongly-signed (a probe, or a secret rotation mid-flight); missing = no bearer at all. Both agent endpoints are public, so a low invalid/missing background rate is internet noise; token_expired never is.

panels.title: Support answers lost to an EXPIRED token (24h) — expect 0 (#2473)
panels.description: sum(increase(agent_token_rejected_total{env="$env",channel="support",reason="token_expired"}[24h])) — each one is a customer who asked a question, had it answered by the agent, and received nothing. Non-zero means the agent-token TTL is shorter than how long a paused cloud-agent run takes to resume; the API also logs each at ERROR. This is the exact #2473 failure, made visible.

title: WifiHaven — Support (Plain)
